0.content:
Wriothesley was taken in as an abandoned infant by a "host family", a loving couple who raised many children together. As each child grew up, they were placed with "families of greater means" and new young children arrived. He considered himself extremely lucky, and so did his siblings. Then he learned the truth: the children were raised "as livestock" and sold, and those who did not sell or who discovered the secret were "disposed of". He was not the first to find out. Too young and weak to fight adults, he fled, survived on the streets and came back armed. He killed both parents and set the remaining children free. He told the Traveler that his parents had built "a facade of joy" and kept power through cruelty, which is why the Beret Society struck him so hard.

He nearly died that night. His Character Story remembers his blood pooling with theirs and how revolting he found the likeness. He has since seen his old companions' names in the court records and chose not to contact them, believing they would rather forget.

1.content:
He woke handcuffed to a hospital bed. Asked his name, he took "Wriothesley" from an old person's obituary rather than keep the name his foster parents had given him. At trial he confessed everything and added details so there was no room for argument, yet lawyers still debated orphan precedents and clemency. Furina left early, bored by his guilty plea. When the official recording his sentence asked his birthday, he answered "...Today": his official birthday, November 23, is that day.

He jokes that a long, hard-to-pronounce name helps you escape the Gardes, and that he must keep sending Furina fine tea to make up for disappointing an Archon. Furina recalls the tea as exquisite.

2.content:
When Wriothesley arrived, Meropide's Credit Coupons bought almost anything: drugs, fixed fights, loyalty, even a life. The administrator of the day used the Coupons to control inmates. Wriothesley built capital in the unregulated underground fights, invested it, and quietly held more Coupons than the rest of the Fortress combined, along with a reputation for fairness. The administrator emptied his account in one night. Wriothesley turned that into a cause and publicly challenged him to a duel "in the name of fairness, justice, and order"; no inmate or guard objected. The administrator fled, sparing Wriothesley more blood on his hands, on the very day his sentence ended. With no one left to sign his exit papers, he walked into the central office and took over.

The wiki infers, from the parallel wording of Cashflow Supervision's and Moment of Cessation's descriptions, that agents of the Harbinger Pantalone introduced the Coupons as an experiment in alternative currency; this is not stated outright, and Wriothesley's own story says only that they have been the Fortress's currency for "a very long time".

3.content:
Sigewinne, the Melusine head nurse, has known Wriothesley since he arrived as a scrawny teenager who refused anaesthetic for stitches ("an impressive little grown-up"). She sometimes slipped it into his tea and stitched him while he slept. He calls her a nurse with every virtue of her profession and enforces an unwritten rule: anyone rude to her is punished extra harshly. She nags him about drinking too much tea; he says her milkshakes taste of "desolation". She and her Melusine friends bet on who can put the most stickers on his things, and he pretends not to mind, because he does not.

For years she wrote to Neuvillette about "the young man", after the Iudex replied asking her to take close care of him. When Wriothesley found out, he called her a spy placed by "our dear Iudex", then told her to keep writing. In Sigewinne's story quest (4.7) he sent her on a surface vacation, approved her joining the doppelganger escape investigation over Morgane's hesitation, and went with Neuvillette to her late teacher's grave.

4.content:
Neuvillette presided over the young Wriothesley's case, followed his progress through Sigewinne's letters, and later conferred the title of Duke. At the ceremony he seemed more pleased than Wriothesley himself: "You have found something you wish to do at last, I see." He calls Wriothesley trustworthy, says he fought hard for the title, and will not explain further. They now cooperate as peers. Neuvillette arranged the Traveler's undercover stay, sealed the Primordial Sea at the gate, and works cases with the Duke.

Wriothesley once found the Iudex standing drenched in the rain outside the Palais and held an umbrella over him, puzzled by his distressed thanks. During the Kiara case (Neuvillette's story quest, 4.1) he produced the inmate Domenico and told the grieving Neuvillette he was overthinking it: today's Fontainians are not those of the past. He believes the Iudex "cannot show concern for anyone".

In the limited 5.6 Whirling Waltz event, Neuvillette pointed out that his ducal papers entitle him to benefits when buying property in the Court. In 6.3, during the Lantern Rite event period, they met in Liyue Harbor, where Wriothesley complimented the Iudex's new Melusine-made outfit and offered to take his overflow of Melusine gifts.

key: If a man will not work
5.comment: Wriothesley: The hidden rules of the Fortress
5.content:
The Fortress is legally autonomous: its inmates are technically exiles, and the Court has little oversight beyond the Gardes it lends. It is also a vast factory, so Wriothesley runs it on "Mora and manpower" and gladly meets the Maison Gestion's strict paperwork for his best customer, the Palais. He set three unwritten rules to teach inmates the worth of health and Coupons. Work non-stop and a mysterious restorative meal (Sigewinne's secret cooking) appears. Bet on both fighters in the Ring and you are served a blood-red test flavour of Fonta. And mistreat the head nurse at your peril. Many inmates choose to stay after their sentences end.

In 4.1 he made the Traveler answer these rules to win Lyney's siblings back. The Traveler solved the first two and missed the third.

6.comment: Wriothesley: The sluice gate and the Wingalet
6.content:
Only the Administrator may enter the Fortress's forbidden zone, where a giant sluice gate stands. Its gauge never moved when he first saw it; over the past year it crept into the red. After Freminet was poisoned by Primordial Seawater, Wriothesley concluded the gate was holding back the Primordial Sea from swallowing Fontaine. He explained that the first Fortress was built by repentant exiles under the old Hydro Archon Egeria to guard this secret. Inspired by Remurian legend, he had his technical consultants Jurieu (once Edwin Eastinghouse's assistant) and Lourvine build a huge escape ship, the Wingalet, and kept it secret to avoid a riot. When the gate failed he froze the surge, Clorinde shot the control panel to drop the backup gates, and he sent the Traveler for Neuvillette.

He bet Clorinde that Neuvillette would come alone, and won. When the prophecy's flood came (4.2), the Wingalet joined the rescue efforts, then went back into storage, with its builders publicly credited so attention stayed off him.

His story "The Wingalet": he had swum in the sea and seen his skin flush red, and told no one. He thought of humanity as "seashells to be smashed upon the seashore" by history's waves and prepared anyway, without much faith in the ship. In 6.7 he rented the Wingalet out during the Fontinalia film festival to pay its maintenance (limited event).

7.comment: Wriothesley: The Vision and the title of Duke
7.content:
On registration day a palm-sized glass ball fell out of his pocket with his sentencing slip: a Cryo Vision he had never noticed receiving. The stern old registrar gasped, said nothing, and wrote "Hide it well" in the margin of his papers; he never saw her again. Knowing from the streets that what you own can be stolen while you sleep, he sewed the Vision between the layers of his clothes with fine wire. He heard of two or three Vision thefts and grim rumours about the victims. For years he pretended to have no divine favour. Only when the Palais invited him to receive the title of Duke did he take it out again. It felt lighter and smaller than before, and he hung it on his coat. He declined the elaborate investiture ceremony and, after many workdays of correspondence, simply signed for the certificates.

Clorinde once asked whether his title was bought; he rummaged through three drawers for the citation ("excellent management", "leading tax contributor") and declared it a good guess. It was a joke: titles cannot be bought in Fontaine.

8.content:
Clorinde visits on business, takes tea in his office and trades deadpan jabs with him. He paid her "good Mora" to come down for "field work" in the Primordial Sea crisis, wanting an independent and exceptionally capable ally. She carried Freminet out of tainted water and held the failing gate with him. He calls her "the best Champion Duelist you can find" and has never fought her, "because there's never been a need for it". She thinks he must be highly capable to keep the Fortress stable and suspects he keeps quiet about some methods.

During the limited 4.4 Lantern Rite event, Clorinde bought Liyue tea to pay off a spur-of-the-moment bet she lost to him. She says he gets invested in bets but does not care what he wins. Neuvillette delivered it, along with his own joke gift of an engraved stone "legal codex".

9.comment: Wriothesley: The House of the Hearth's infiltration
9.content:
Arlecchino's House of the Hearth planted informants among the Fortress's inmates and guards. Wriothesley caught and removed them, which he admits was "kind of an intentional provocation". The House answered by sending Lyney, Lynette and Freminet with the Traveler's intake. He knew who they were from the start, first thought they were looking for Childe, then realised Lyney wanted the forbidden zone. He moved Lynette out of the infirmary and locked the tunnel exit behind Freminet so Lyney could not follow him into danger. Lyney accused him of kidnapping and demanded his siblings back. Wriothesley offered their safety in exchange for a talk with "Father"; Lyney called it blackmail and lunged, and Sigewinne's tranquilliser dart dropped him. Afterwards Wriothesley let the Traveler share what he had shown them with the siblings.

He wonders whether the Fatui sent children because they saw them as disposable, "or because they knew I wouldn't have it in me to let them come to serious harm."

10.content:
In his story quest (Reborn in the Land of Grievances, 4.1), Wriothesley investigated the Beret Society, a club of model inmates. Its founder Dougier controlled members with thorns hidden under their berets that injected a fear solution, "Aqua Doloris", and was stockpiling decommissioned Gardemeks to overthrow him. Wriothesley told him he could not tell "sharing" from "looting" and that the Fortress is "a place for rebirth". He wrecked the meka, dodged Dougier's shots behind an ice wall and, when Dougier aimed at Paimon, pinned him by the throat. Reminded that unauthorised punishment is forbidden, he answered that the rules exist to keep people like Dougier in check, and that the Duke needs no justification. He then apologised to every member in person and blamed himself for what happened under his watch.

His punishment for Dougier: leave him in the dark, imagining what is coming, while Wriothesley asks the victims what was done to them. Two days later the thorns were confirmed removable. Avice and Faissolle, who had met in the Society, asked to marry inside the Fortress and to stay after their sentences. He agreed to the first prison wedding: "I'll always take a genuine expression of faith over any obligation to obey."

11.content: The Fortress cooperates with the Spina di Rosula only on supplies and logistics. Wriothesley holds Navia in high regard but keeps the two organisations apart to honour the agreement he made with her late father Callas. Callas, who once refused a barony himself, assumed "Duke" was a hollow title until he met him and decided Wriothesley was "far more worldly than he looks". Navia finds negotiating with him exhausting; Clorinde told her to cooperate within the agreement but not to trust everything he says.

12.content: His mechanical gauntlets have gone through many versions. The first was a wrist-mounted nail launcher he built on the streets for his return to the foster home; it broke in that fight and could not be saved. In the Fortress's old ring, with no fixed venue or rules, he kept modifying them because a trick used once could be turned against you, and rivals stole or wrecked them. Later, with better materials, he stopped relying on chemicals to power them and got help from researchers of the Fontaine Research Institute, who enjoy explaining mechanics while complaining about the Institute's mishaps. Today he rarely fights matches and saves the gauntlets for the trickiest problems; they "no longer took life".

13.comment: Wriothesley: The Cacucu smuggling case (5.6 event)
13.content: During the limited 5.6 Whirling Waltz event, Natlanese visitors came to Fontaine after their war with the Abyss. Wriothesley and Neuvillette were discussing a smuggling case when a panicked talking bird, Cacucu, flew into the Palais Mermonia. Neuvillette reinterpreted the flying-object rules for him, and Cacucu stayed with Wriothesley, who managed to teach him only "good morning". With Kinich, Ororon, Ifa and Cacucu he caught the go-between Argenteau, told him he faced a heavy sentence in an international case, and offered leniency for cooperation. That led them to the mastermind Angoulvant. Along the way he mused about wanting a pet and buying property now the flood prophecy was over, and joked that if he knew every law he would not have ended up in the Fortress.

14.comment: Wriothesley: Nod-Krai business and Barbeloth's reading
14.content: In his 2025 birthday letter (6.1) Wriothesley mentioned business in Nod-Krai. He sampled the local food, watched a few no-holds-barred underground fights to read the fighters' characters, and stayed longer than planned; the Fortress ran itself while he was away. In the 6.7 World Quest Witch's Revelation: Warden's Instruction, he visited Barbeloth's fortune-telling booth on Columbina's recommendation, bringing Conch Madeleines, and charmed Alice over the link. He drew the upright Emperor ("eternal dominion and unshakable authority") and suggested that his surroundings, not he, were what was changing. He said the Nod-Krai trip had left him watching the news from there and that, under an unusually bright moon, he felt "the world is changing". He then asked how a prophecy ensures its own fulfilment if its subject rebels on hearing it; when the Traveler suggested "blowing up the Fortress of Meropide" as the example, he went along with it ("Sure, let's go with that").

15.content: During the limited 6.7 Fontinalia festival, Wriothesley and Chevreuse arranged supervised time on the surface for well-behaved inmates. The Traveler introduced their Nod-Krai friend Columbina, who punched his arm as a "gesture of friendship"; the Traveler punched the other, and he remarked that they knew how to pick friends. He offered the Wingalet as a filming location. He had rented it out to pay for its upkeep and because seeing their work used is good rehabilitation for the inmates who maintain it. The renter was Sandrone, posing as "Marionette" and addressed by him as "Miss Guillotin", who had turned it into an aquarium; he asked to keep some of the installations for the inmates. Inmates Veronique and Baptiste credited him with fighting for their festival leave. He told them their kind of "justice" was one people could respect.

16.content: In the 6.4 anecdote "Wriothesley: Quite the Win", guards caught a strange "Melusine" under the Fortress searchlights: Pahsiv, a vishap who calls Neuvillette her "New Valet" and Wriothesley "Wrio". He dove for Tidalga to feed her himself, warned her that anglerfish use lights as bait, and broadcast a missing-person notice that brought Neuvillette. He told the Traveler this is why it is worth staying alive: to hear stories from those who have lived longer. He then planned to have the Research Institute add identity checks to the searchlights.

17.content: In the 6.3 World Quest A Gift From the Sea Spirits, in a scene available during that version's Lantern Rite event period, Wriothesley and Sigewinne met Neuvillette, the Traveler and Paimon at Liyue's Lantern Rite. He talked Neuvillette out of hanging Xiao Lanterns over the Fortress: they would not fly high inside its walls, and the inmates' wishes would hardly be in the public interest. He regretted not buying Fortune Coin packets to hand out, and offered to treat everyone to a meal with Paimon leading the way. He said Liyue has a flavour quite unlike Fontaine's, and not just in the tea.

18.content: In 4.1 the Traveler and Paimon were "sentenced" to the Fortress for eating a cake meant for Furina, a cover so they could investigate Childe's disappearance there for Neuvillette. Wriothesley met them with a squad of Gardemeks and gave them the tour himself. After the gate crisis he let them come and go freely, kept their cell and daily meal, and asked only that they file the forms when the 45 days were up. When they did, he signed their release, told them the tremors came from the surface, not the seabed, and, when Sigewinne asked them to pass on her regards to Neuvillette, added that he hoped the busy Palais had not been overwhelmed. His voice line: "They say it's best to begin a friendship when there's no conflict of interest. Seems like the appropriate time has come."
